title: Definite Integration
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus?
cards.a: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = [ F(x) ]_a^b = F(b) - F(a), where F'(x) = f(x).
cards.hint: No arbitrary constant '+ c' is needed in definite integration because c - c = 0 cancels out.

cards.q: Property 1 (Dummy Variable) and Property 2 (Limit Reversal)?
cards.a:
P1: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(t) dt (value is independent of integration variable name).
P2: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = - ∫_b^a f(x) dx (reversing limits negates the integral).
cards.hint: Also note P3: ∫_a^a f(x) dx = 0.

cards.q: Property 4 (Splitting the Interval)?
cards.a: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^c f(x) dx + ∫_c^b f(x) dx, for any real number c.
cards.hint: Crucial for evaluating piecewise functions, modulus |x|, and greatest integer functions [x].

cards.q: Property 5 (King's Rule): The Master Property of Definite Integrals?
cards.a: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b - x) dx.
cards.hint: Replace x by (lower limit + upper limit - x). Adds to original I to cancel difficult denominators!

cards.q: Property 6 (Queen's Rule / Special King's Rule with limit 0 to a)?
cards.a: ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a - x) dx.
cards.hint: The single most tested property in Maharashtra Board exams!

cards.q: MHT-CET Super Shortcut 1: King's Rule quotient formula?
cards.hint: Instant 5-second answer! Simply take (upper limit - lower limit) / 2.

cards.q: Classic Evaluation: ∫_0^(π/2) [ sinⁿ x / (sinⁿ x + cosⁿ x) ] dx?
cards.a: = (π/2 - 0) / 2 = π/4, for ANY real power n (e.g. n = 1, 2, 1/2, 2026).
cards.hint: Also holds for cosⁿ x, tanⁿ x / (1 + tanⁿ x), and 1 / (1 + cotⁿ x).

cards.q: Property 7: Symmetric limits from -a to +a (Even and Odd Functions)?
cards.a:
∫_(-a)^a f(x) dx = 2 ∫_0^a f(x) dx (if f(-x) = f(x), EVEN function)
∫_(-a)^a f(x) dx = 0 (if f(-x) = -f(x), ODD function).
cards.hint: Always check symmetry: if limits are [-a, a], test f(-x) first before doing any integration!

cards.q: MHT-CET Odd Function Trap: Evaluate ∫_(-1)^1 [ x³ + x cos x + tan⁵ x + 1 ] dx?
cards.hint: Separate the even part (1) from odd parts (x³, x cos x, tan⁵ x). Don't waste time on odd terms.

cards.q: Property 8: Limits from 0 to 2a (Upper limit halving property)?
cards.hint: Allows halving the upper limit from 2a to a when the function is symmetric about a.

cards.q: Classic Result: Value of ∫_0^(π/2) ln(sin x) dx and ∫_0^(π/2) ln(cos x) dx?
cards.hint: Frequently tested 4-mark proof in HSC Board exams and direct formula in MHT-CET.

cards.q: Classic Result: Value of ∫_0^π [ x / (a² cos² x + b² sin² x) ] dx?
cards.hint: First remove x using King's rule: ∫_0^π x f(x) dx = (π/2) ∫_0^π f(x) dx.

cards.q: Shortcut to evaluate modulus integrals ∫_a^b |x - c| dx (where a ≤ c ≤ b)?
cards.a: Area of two right isosceles triangles: = (1/2) (c - a)² + (1/2) (b - c)².
cards.hint: Geometric shortcut saves splitting the integral into two separate cases.

cards.q: How to evaluate integrals involving Greatest Integer Function [x]?
cards.a: Split the integral at EVERY integer boundary within the limits, where [x] takes constant integer values.

cards.q: Periodic Function Properties for period T (i.e. f(x + T) = f(x))?
cards.a:
1. ∫_0^(nT) f(x) dx = n ∫_0^T f(x) dx  (for n ∈ Z)
2. ∫_a^(a + nT) f(x) dx = n ∫_0^T f(x) dx (independent of a)
3. ∫_(a + nT)^(b + nT) f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(x) dx.
cards.hint: Pull integer multiples n of the fundamental period T outside the integral!

cards.q: Leibniz Rule for differentiation under the integral sign?
cards.a: d/dx [ ∫_u(x)^v(x) f(t) dt ] = f(v(x)) · v'(x) - f(u(x)) · u'(x).
cards.hint: Used to compute limits of 0/0 form involving integrals via L'Hospital's Rule.

cards.q: Definite Integral as the Limit of a Sum (Riemann Sum)?
cards.hint: Replace r/n with x, 1/n with dx, and limit of sum with ∫_0^1.

cards.q: Wallis' Reduction Formula for ∫_0^(π/2) sinⁿ x dx = ∫_0^(π/2) cosⁿ x dx?
cards.hint: Multiply by π/2 ONLY when n is an EVEN positive integer.

cards.q: TRAP: What must you always do to the limits when substituting x = g(t)?
cards.a: You MUST convert the x-limits to corresponding t-limits using t = g⁻¹(x) immediately before proceeding with the integration.
cards.hint: Never keep old limits after substitution! #1 source of lost marks in definite integrals.

cards.q: Value of ∫_0^1 x (1 - x)ⁿ dx?
cards.hint: Apply Property 6: replace x by (1 - x), giving ∫_0^1 (1 - x) xⁿ dx = 1/(n+1) - 1/(n+2).

cards.q: Value of ∫_0^(π/4) ln(1 + tan x) dx?
cards.hint: Use King's rule: tan(π/4 - x) = (1 - tan x)/(1 + tan x). Standard Board problem!

cards.q: Integral of fractional part {x} = x - [x] from 0 to n (n ∈ N)?
cards.hint: {x} is periodic with period 1; area of each unit saw-tooth triangle is 1/2.

cards.q: Difference between Definite Integral and Area?
cards.a:
A definite integral ∫_a^b f(x) dx is a net signed quantity (can be positive, zero, or negative).
Area is a geometric measure and is ALWAYS strictly non-negative (≥ 0).
cards.hint: If a curve dips below x-axis, the integral subtracts the region, whereas area adds its absolute value.

cards.q: Value of ∫_(-π/2)^(π/2) sin⁷ x dx and ∫_(-π/2)^(π/2) cos² x dx?
cards.a:
∫_(-π/2)^(π/2) sin⁷ x dx = 0 (odd function).
∫_(-π/2)^(π/2) cos² x dx = 2 ∫_0^(π/2) cos² x dx = 2 · (1/2 · π/2) = π/2 (even function).
cards.hint: Check odd/even nature instantly to save calculation time.
Lower limit a = 2, upper limit b = 8 ⇒ a + b = 10. Direct application of MHT-CET Shortcut 1!
